title: 10 Best AI Agent Integration Platforms
summary: Composio, Pipedream, Arcade, Zapier and six more on per-agent identity, per-user permissions and audit. First-party, no scores, checked 29 October 2026.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


**Connector count stopped being the number that matters in this category once agents started taking real actions instead of just answering questions.** Once an agent can send an email, open a pull request, or write to a database, the decisive questions are which agent is doing it, whose authority it's borrowing, and whether that specific action is even allowed.


Most platforms in this ranking still lead with a tool count in the tens of thousands. On 2026-10-29 Composio advertised "20,000+ tools", Zapier "66,000+ triggers and actions", StackOne "36,000+ actions". Those numbers measure reach, and they move fast: all three were smaller when we first published this page in August 2026. They say nothing about whether a shared agent gets different permissions for an intern than for an administrator, or whether a denied attempt leaves a trace anyone can find later.


Reach still matters plenty. A platform with three tools nobody needs is useless no matter how well governed it is. But reach and control are two different things to evaluate, and most platforms on this list are noticeably stronger at one than the other.


We rank ourselves first, and we say so upfront. We give no platform a score, including ours, and nothing here is independent. Read the individual entries for where each platform genuinely leads, including the entries that aren't us, and check the linked sources before a number from this page ends up in your decision. There is also a third answer we take seriously below: for one or two stable APIs, calling the provider directly beats buying any platform on this list.
